conditions: Control Parallel Lives when Dragon Fodder resolves; pay {1}{R}.
explanation: The replacement makes four Goblins from the one creation event.

conditions: Control Procession before Raise the Alarm resolves.
explanation: Two Soldier tokens become four through a mandatory replacement.

conditions: Control both permanents; Ballista must survive entry; pay {4} for each activation.
explanation: Ballista's activated effect places two counters instead of one. Removing a counter to deal damage is a cost and is not doubled.

conditions: Ballista is a creature you control; pay {4} per activation.
explanation: The additive replacement makes a placement of one counter become two. It works by adding one, rather than multiplying the number.

conditions: Control Season and a legal creature target through resolution; start with zero counters for the example.
explanation: The first placement gives two counters. Doubling would place two more, so replacement adds four; the creature ends with six.
gap: Phase 2 sequential counter effects and rules-level double action

conditions: Soul Warden is on the battlefield when Dragon Fodder resolves.
explanation: Creating these creature tokens puts them onto the battlefield; Warden triggers for each.

conditions: Control Fireweaver when the Treasure enters; casting or flashback requires its respective cost.
explanation: Treasure is a noncreature artifact. It triggers Fireweaver without needing to be tapped or sacrificed.

conditions: Have a card to discard and pay {3}{R}; permanents must be present during resolution.
explanation: Discarding happens at cast time. Both synergies depend on the same later Treasure-creation effect; applying both claims does not duplicate the inventory record.

conditions: You control the nontoken Wall, which remains a legal target; the return is not prevented.
explanation: The Wall becomes a new battlefield object and its own entry trigger draws one card.

conditions: Wall is another legal nontoken creature; owner receives it tapped; ideally own and control it to draw; pay {2}{C} each time.
explanation: Displacer can repeatedly blink Wall if new mana is supplied. The controller of the new Wall gets its draw trigger.
gap: Phase 2 blink parser and Phase 3 compound mana-cost renewal

conditions: Returning a creature to the battlefield is the only creature movement under test.
explanation: Cloudshift itself is an instant. Its returned creature is not cast and cannot trigger the creature-spell cast ability.

conditions: You control Waste Not and cast Big Score.
explanation: The caster discards their own card, so Waste Not's opponent-discard triggers do not fire.

conditions: Keep the outlet and payoff as package roles; an eligible creature under your control and a legal player target are needed.
explanation: Sacrifice can cause death but the pair has no distinct replenishable or expendable fodder while preserving the two roles.

conditions: Control all three or start Skeleton in your graveyard with mana; choose a legal player target; receive priority after each step.
explanation: Sacrifice Skeleton, resolve the death trigger and pay {1}{B} to return Skeleton tapped. The cycle expends fresh mana every time.

conditions: Evaluate immediate battlefield renewal during the opponent's turn. Gutterbones cannot use its own-turn activation or be cast then.
explanation: The fixture lacks a verified battlefield-return path; hand return cannot directly renew the on-board resource.

conditions: Cast and resolve Raise; spend distinct tokens for each activation; keep Blood Artist and a legal player target available.
explanation: The exact outlet consumes one Soldier per use. Two Soldiers permit two activations; they do not renew on their own.

conditions: Keep Artist and Priest for future cycles; only one other creature is initially available.
explanation: The future mana payment cannot pay costs before the ability resolves. Skeleton cannot be spent twice as one activation cost.
gap: Phase 2 multi-object sacrifice costs; Phase 3 multiplicity closure

conditions: Ayara may pay its tap cost only while untapped and after the control restriction is satisfied or with haste. Fodder must be another black creature.
explanation: Skeleton qualifies as black fodder, but pay its return cost each time and renew Ayara's tap before using it again.
gap: Phase 2 typed color restriction on sacrifice costs

conditions: Morbid Opportunist has not triggered this turn. Preserve it and pay {1}{B} for each Skeleton return.
explanation: Further Skeleton deaths in the same turn do not draw additional cards through this trigger. Repeat the payoff across turns.

conditions: Aesi is the commander; only Lay of the Land's resolution is credited.
explanation: Putting the searched land into hand creates no battlefield entry, even though it might later be played.

conditions: Aesi is on the battlefield and Rampant Growth finds a basic land; drawing is optional.
explanation: The basic land enters tapped under your control and Aesi can trigger. Aesi belongs to the command zone configuration.

conditions: Need an available land and a legal land-play window on your turn. Aesi is on the battlefield.
explanation: Explore permits an extra land play but does not itself move a land to the battlefield.

conditions: Young Pyromancer must be on the battlefield when Opt is cast.
explanation: The cast trigger is stacked above Opt, so countering Opt does not undo the trigger.

conditions: Magecraft creature on battlefield; Reverberate targets an instant or sorcery still legal at resolution.
explanation: Casting Reverberate and copying a target spell are separate qualifying events.

conditions: Control Young Pyromancer and cast Reverberate normally.
explanation: Casting Reverberate triggers Pyromancer only once. The spell copy is put directly on the stack and does not create an extra cast trigger.

conditions: Swords resolves against a legal creature.
explanation: Swords moves its target from battlefield to exile. Directly moving it there does not create a death event.

conditions: Boots are attached before Wrath resolves; assume no other applicable protection.
explanation: Hexproof restricts targeting by opponents. Wrath specifies no target, so it still destroys the equipped creature.

conditions: Double Major copies a legal creature spell you control and the copy resolves.
explanation: The copy enters as a token without a token-creation event. Parallel Lives does not replace this entry.

conditions: Structural package is scoped to the lineup. In the negative board-state variant, Rest in Peace is active; no card or token reaches the graveyard.
explanation: The builder must keep the graveyard prerequisite on its conditional package. That prerequisite cannot be met while Rest in Peace applies.
gap: Runtime global-board replacements are outside the static artifact; conditional requirements must survive

conditions: Start with Skeleton, Altar and Plunderer under your control. The death trigger resolves before spending the Treasure.
explanation: Altar makes {C}{C}; Treasure pays {B}; spend {C}{B} returning Skeleton. One colorless mana remains per cycle.
gap: Phase 3 colored resource ledger and closed-loop solver

conditions: Same start as Altar loop; choose mana for the generic payment with Altar and black with Treasure.
explanation: Both resources are consumed; initial permanents and fodder are restored. Repeat death and entry events arbitrarily often without creating surplus mana.

conditions: No black mana source and no treasure producer. Only the candidate closed loop is scored.
explanation: Two colorless mana cannot pay a black symbol. Altar plus Skeleton alone cannot restore its starting state.

conditions: Control both; Kiki-Jiki untapped and able to activate. Conscripts is a legal nonlegendary creature target; each token's triggered target is Kiki-Jiki.
explanation: Copy Conscripts, resolve its ETB to untap Kiki-Jiki, then repeat. You can choose any finite count before end-step sacrifice triggers.
gap: Phase 2 copy-to-entry/untap relations and Phase 3 loop solver

conditions: Control both, start with one qualifying life event and a legal opponent target. Assume ordinary finite life totals and uninterrupted triggers.
explanation: The trigger chain renews without paying mana, but opponent elimination supplies a terminal state. A mandatory loop with no reachable end can instead draw the game.
gap: Phase 2 life-loss observers and Phase 3 terminal-state modeling

conditions: Resolve Exsanguinate with X positive against a player with The Wanderer.
explanation: The Wanderer prevents noncombat damage. Exsanguinate directly decreases life totals without a damage event.

conditions: A legal target remains and Fog has resolved this turn.
explanation: Fog prevents combat damage. Bolt deals damage from a spell rather than the combat damage step.

conditions: Teysa's color identity is white and black. Black Lotus is Commander-banned in the pinned snapshot.
explanation: The pool excludes the banned Lotus and off-color Dragon Fodder before graph analysis.

conditions: Start with untapped Oven and Familiar on the battlefield or with a Food to seed it. Oven needs to untap before the next activation.
explanation: Sacrifice Cat to Oven to make Food, then sacrifice Food to Cat's return. Both costs use different objects. No same-turn automatic untap exists.
gap: Phase 2 Food-cost join and Phase 3 turn-based renewal

conditions: Woe Strider enters and creates a distinct Goat; all relevant permanents remain and a legal player target exists.
explanation: The same owned card provides the generator and outlet abilities. The Goat is a separate object consumed once; Woe Strider is counted only once.
gap: Phase 3 single-card multiple-role closure across distinct abilities

conditions: Lantern exiles a creature card already in a graveyard; Lantern is an artifact, not a creature.
explanation: The exiled card does not move from battlefield to graveyard. Sacrificing the noncreature Lantern does not qualify for Blood Artist either.

conditions: Wall remains a legal target. Rebound requires Ephemerate to have been cast from hand and resolve, then be cast once from exile at the next upkeep.
explanation: The two paths share one Wall entry ability. Ephemerate supplies one bounded second cast, with neither ongoing renewal nor a self-sustaining claim.

conditions: You control the Orchard, Parallel Lives and Fireweaver. An opponent is the legal target of the forced token trigger.
explanation: The opponent creates and controls a nonartifact Spirit. Your token doubler and artifact-entry payoff do not apply.

conditions: Gisa is ready and untapped; pay black mana and sacrifice a different creature of positive power. Keep Warden in play and supply new fodder, mana and a ready tap for each further use.
explanation: The sacrificed creature is used once as a cost. Gisa creates a variable number of Zombies only on resolution; at zero power no Zombie enters to trigger Warden.
